title: Starter Tooling Journey — accelerator notes & quickstart skeleton
body:
Purpose

Short: create a minimal, repeatable quickstart flow and a companion starter-tooling kit that any engineer can use to get to a working Redwood API integration in ~10-20 minutes. This doc collects decisions, sprint tasks, and the skeletal copy/code that will become the first draft of the quickstart.

Audience
- New engineering adopters (first integration)
- Internal solutions engineers and SEs running demos
- Developer advocates and docs authors who will iterate on phrasing

Goals and success metrics (MVP)
- Goal: time-to-first-successful-API-call & simple local dev loop under 20 minutes for a new user with a git clone and the token.
- Metric 1: 80% of test cohort completes the quickstart end-to-end without help.
- Metric 2: < 5 questions raised per 100 quickstart runs in first month (measured via support tags).

Constraints / boundaries
- Keep the quickstart mono-repo minimal: single README, one example in Node (JS/TS) and one in Python. No extra dependencies.
- Focus on the hosted API path only for MVP (no Dedicated/Private branching).
- Do not require Docker for the first pass.

High-level flow (user story)
1) Sign up / get token (assume user has token or free credits).
2) git clone starter-tooling repo
3) open README, copy token to .env
4) run the single command: npm run start or python run_quickstart.py
5) see a simple text-generation result and a small example of streaming tokens + explanation of costs in console
6) next steps: how to move to advanced topics (batching, rollouts, embeddings).

Quickstart skeleton (README sections)
- Title and 1-line: what they will build
- Prereqs: node >= 16 or python 3.10, token, editor
- Get a token: link to signup and note about free credits and rate limits
- Clone + install commands (copy/paste)
- Configure: how to put token in .env or environment variable (export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...)
body_extra:
- Run: example commands, expected output, troubleshooting (common errors: 401, CORS during browser example, network timeout)
- Explanation: what the example does in 4 bullets (calls, model, params, cost)
- Next steps: link to SDK reference, streaming guide, prompt labs, embedding quickstart

Minimal code examples (to include inline in README)
Node (minimal):
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const r = await fetch(process.env.REDWOOD_API_URL || 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rw-small-1', prompt: 'Write a 2-line haiku about debugging' })
  });
  console.log(await r.text());
})();

Python (minimal):
import os, requests
resp = requests.post(
  os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_URL', 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'),
  headers={'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}", 'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
  json={'model': 'rw-small-1', 'prompt': 'List three quick tips for prompt clarity'}
)
print(resp.json())

Operations checklist for the repo
- [ ] Add CI smoke test that runs both examples with a mock token or integration token in a protected secret. (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Add a small e2e test that asserts the text shape and cost metadata are returned (owner: Leah)
- [ ] Add a minimal telemetry hook example showing how to time requests and log token counts (owner: Dan)

UX / copy notes (docs team)
- Keep language concrete and action-oriented: "Copy this, paste this, run this" rather than theoretical descriptions.
- Include a single screenshot of terminal with the expected output and a callout explaining where to find the token in the Console.
- Provide one short paragraph explaining cost tradeoffs for the chosen model in plain english ("~1–3c per 1k tokens for this model, depends on length").

Edge cases and troubleshooting (short list)
- 401 Unauthorized: check token env var and surrounding whitespace in .env.
- Slow response / timeout: recommend short prompt and retry with increased timeout.
- CORS errors when using browser snippet: call out that the quickstart is server-side only for MVP, add a browser example in v2 with the correct CORS proxy approach.

Open questions (to decide in next sync)
- Do we include a streaming example in the main quickstart or a separate advanced page? (tradeoff: streaming has async complexity for beginners).
- Do we include a basic embedding example, or keep that as a separate "use-case" quickstart?
- What is the official minimal model to use for public quickstarts (rw-small-1 vs rw-medium-1)? Need cost/throughput guidance from Applied ML.

Deliverables for the next two sprints
- Sprint A (2 weeks): initial repo + README + node+python examples + CI smoke (owner: Marco)
- Sprint B (2 weeks): docs polish + screenshot + telemetry example + integration test + design review (owner: Leah)

Notes from convo with SEs (1/23 meeting)
- SEs want a single canonical demo that can be forked for customer PoCs. Keep it intentionally small so SEs can copy/paste pieces into demos.
- Include a short "how to demo in 5 minutes" script for SEs.

Reference links and tickets
- Confluence starter index: confluence:DEVX/Starter-Tooling-Index
- Jira ticket for repo creation: JIRA:DX-347
- GitHub starter templates PR: github:infra/starter-templates#45

Next steps (action items)
- Aisha: draft README and push an initial commit to a draft repo by 2025-01-20.
- Marco: add CI smoke and create DX-347 subtasks by 2025-01-22.
- Leah: draft screenshot and the "5 minute demo" script by 2025-01-28.

Quick capture: informal TODOs and scribbles
- Consider a single-file runnable example that prints cost per-call afterward (so users see immediate economics).
- Keep dependencies zero where possible; prefer fetch/requests over heavy SDKs in the first example.
- v2: add a "migrate to SDK" short section showing how to swap fetch/request with official SDK call.

End of doc.
